Green Tamales (Tamales Verdes)

Served at: Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe

Makes about 20-25 tamalesPrep 1 hour 30 minCook 1 hour 30 min

Green Tamales, or Tamales Verdes, are a festive and flavorful dish, deeply ingrained in Mexican culinary traditions, especially during celebrations. For the Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe on December 12th, these savory parcels filled with tender chicken and a vibrant salsa verde are a beloved staple, symbolizing community and devotion as families gather to honor the Virgin of Guadalupe.

Ingredients

  • 30-40 dried corn husks
  • 2 pounds (900g) tomatillos, husked and rinsed
  • 3-4 serrano peppers (or 2-3 jalapeños for milder), stems removed
  • 1/2 medium white onion, roughly chopped
  • 3 cloves garlic, peeled
  • 1/2 cup (120ml) fresh cilantro, roughly chopped
  • 1 tablespoon vegetable oil
  • Salt to taste
  • 3 cups (about 450g) cooked chicken, shredded
  • 4 cups (480g) masa harina for tamales (not regular masa flour)
  • 2 teaspoons baking powder
  • 2 teaspoons salt
  • 1 1/2 cups (340g) lard or vegetable shortening, at room temperature
  • 3 1/2 cups (840ml) warm chicken broth

Method

  1. Place corn husks in a large bowl or pot, cover with very hot water, and weigh down with a plate to keep them submerged. Let them soak for at least 1 hour, or until pliable.
  2. While husks soak, prepare the salsa verde: Place tomatillos, serrano peppers, onion, and garlic in a medium saucepan. Cover with water and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer for 10-15 minutes, or until tomatillos are soft and have changed to a dull green color.
  3. Drain the vegetables, reserving about 1/2 cup (120ml) of the cooking liquid. Transfer the cooked vegetables to a blender with the fresh cilantro and 1/4 cup (60ml) of the reserved cooking liquid. Blend until smooth, adding more liquid if needed to reach a pourable consistency.
  4. Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Pour in the blended salsa verde (be careful, it may splatter). Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low and cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the salsa has thickened slightly and deepened in color. Season with salt to taste. Let cool slightly.
  5. In a large bowl, combine the shredded cooked chicken with about 1 1/2 to 2 cups (360-480ml) of the prepared salsa verde, or enough to generously coat the chicken. Mix well and set aside.
  6. In a stand mixer with the paddle attachment (or a large bowl with a hand mixer), beat the lard or shortening on medium-high speed until it is light and fluffy, about 3-5 minutes.
  7. In a separate bowl, whisk together the masa harina, baking powder, and 2 teaspoons of salt.
  8. Gradually add the masa harina mixture to the beaten lard, alternating with the warm chicken broth, mixing on low speed until just combined. Increase speed to medium and beat for 5-7 minutes, until the masa is light, fluffy, and resembles a soft dough. To test if the masa is ready, drop a small ball (about 1/2 teaspoon) into a cup of cold water; if it floats, it's ready. If it sinks, beat for a few more minutes and retest.
  9. Drain the softened corn husks and pat them dry with a clean kitchen towel.
  10. To assemble each tamale: Take one corn husk, wider end facing you. Spread about 2-3 tablespoons of masa evenly over the wider part of the husk, leaving about 1 inch (2.5 cm) clear at the top and sides. The masa layer should be about 1/4 inch (0.6 cm) thick.
  11. Place about 1-2 tablespoons of the chicken and salsa verde filling down the center of the masa.
  12. Fold one long side of the husk over the filling, then fold the other long side over, overlapping slightly. Fold the narrow bottom end of the husk up towards the center. Leave the top open.
  13. Repeat with the remaining masa, filling, and corn husks.
  14. Set up a large steamer pot. Add water to just below the steamer basket. Arrange the tamales upright in the steamer basket, open-end facing up, packing them snugly. If you have extra corn husks, you can place them on top of the tamales to help trap steam.
  15. Bring the water to a boil, then reduce heat to medium-low, cover tightly, and steam for 1 hour to 1 hour 30 minutes, or until the masa pulls away easily from the husk. Check water level periodically and add more hot water if needed.
  16. Remove tamales from the steamer and let them rest for 10-15 minutes before serving. This allows them to firm up.

Tips

  • For an extra layer of flavor, you can add a small piece of Oaxaca cheese or Monterey Jack cheese to the chicken filling.
  • Tamales freeze beautifully. Once cooled, wrap them individually in plastic wrap and then place them in a freezer-safe bag for up to 3 months. Reheat by steaming or microwaving.
  • The salsa verde can be made a day in advance to save time on assembly day. Store it in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
